correctness.rationale: A general zero-free cubic factors into three degree-one factors with parameters in the closed unit disk. Expanding elementary symmetric functions gives an exact cosine identity. A phase-independent lower bound splits by the number of radii at least sqrt(3/7). Exact rational Bernstein certificates show strict positivity in the zero-, one-, and three-high cases; in the two-high case a positive quadratic coefficient and an exact nonnegative discriminant complement cover all radii. The latter vanishes only at two unit radii and a third radius 1/4. The three coupling phases then force two factors equal and the short factor antipodal. The extremizer has norm squared 35/8 and first coefficient squared 49/16, ratio 7/10. All exact certificate computations were regenerated by verify.py with CHECK_OK; no numerical sampling substitutes for a proof.

Direct searches for equivalent coefficient inequalities, root parametrizations, and special constants disclosed no dominating result. value.rationale: The degree-three sharp Hardy coefficient constant for zero-free polynomials is a natural finite-dimensional extremal invariant within a classical infinite-dimensional coefficient problem. The calculated constant and full equality classification identify a genuinely mixed root geometry: two coincident boundary roots and a third external antipodal zero, unlike the simple all-boundary quadratic pattern. The exact finite cutoff addresses a natural degree excluded from a current n>=5 framework and gives a precise comparison target for higher-degree or other-norm studies. Its importance is the complete sharp classification of this natural first nontrivial cubic problem, not merely numerical reproducibility.
